events.summary: AAOI fell 13.58% to $105.90 (low $104.88) on about 2.5x normal volume, closing near the day's low. events.summary: Chip stocks sold off from the open as long-term interest rates stayed near multi-decade highs and oil jumped. The 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.37% on Wednesday (highest in 24 years per Investopedia), was near 5.36% Thursday morning, then eased to about 5.23% by the close. WTI crude rose 3.4% to $91.30 and Brent about 3.8% to about $104 on worries about renewed US action against Iran, tanker attacks and Hurricane Isaias. Investopedia also cites Samsung's fall in Korean trading for the morning chip weakness. The Nasdaq fell about 1.3% and the S&P 500 about 0.5%.

events.type: industry: AI-demand news (Financial Times report on OpenAI)
events.summary: During Thursday afternoon trading, the Financial Times reported that OpenAI's annualized revenue was about $20 billion less than previously signaled. The AI trade sold off after it: the Philadelphia chip index fell as much as 4%; Marvell and Arm fell more than 6%, Micron more than 5%, Nvidia nearly 3%. The Yahoo live-blog entry is stamped 18:39 UTC (14:39 ET). AAOI went from about -9% at noon to -13.6% at the close, near its low (timing match, our inference).
events.why_it_matters: OpenAI is one of the biggest buyers of AI computing. If it earns less than thought, investors worry that the spending chain (AI labs to cloud data centers to optical modules) could slow. That would hit AOI's growth thesis, which depends on that spending. It is a sentiment shock, not a reported order cut.

events.summary: Overnight, Lumentum's CEO Michael Hurlston said in an interview in Tokyo that its optical-component capacity is booked by customers through early 2029, driven by AI data-center construction. He added that 'there is still no clear sign of relief for the current supply-demand imbalance', and gave a 12-fold rise in its Greater Tokyo capacity over two years and planned investment of more than $350 million. AAOI traded +5% to +7% before the open ($113.32 at 08:36 ET), opened +6.4%, reached +10.6%, and closed +3.53% at $109.64 while SMH fell 0.65%.

products.name: 800G and 1.6T data-center optical transceivers
products.what_it_is: Plug-in modules that turn a server or switch's electrical signals into laser light and back, so data can travel over glass fibre at 800 or 1,600 gigabits per second.
products.analogy: A translator at each end of a phone line: one side speaks 'electricity', the cable speaks 'light', and the module converts between them in real time.
products.buyers: Large cloud/AI data-center operators ('hyperscalers'), directly or via distributors. AOI's top 10 customers are 99% of revenue, and one distributor owed it $211.0m at Q2 (AOI 10-Q, 2026-08-06, per thesis file). Customer names not disclosed in our sources.
products.how_it_works: Each AI server rack links to switches through many fibre links; every link needs a transceiver at each end. Faster AI clusters move to 800G and then 1.6T modules. AOI makes its own lasers and assembles modules in the US (Houston), Taiwan and China.
products.sales: Units and per-product revenue not disclosed in the Q2 release. Labelled proxies: data-center revenue was 56.1% of Q2 2026 revenue of $191.9m, about $107.7m (our calculation; TradingKey also gives $107.7m). The Q2 release says 800G volume 'more than doubled sequentially'. Total manufacturing capacity was 'approaching 200,000 units per month', with a target of about 650,000 800G and 1.6T units per month by end-2026. Management forecast demand will outpace capacity through mid-2027. TradingKey also cites '800G product revenue $12.8 million', which we could not verify in the release.
products.stage: 800G in volume ramp; 1.6T early production/ramp (Q2 release: 'solid progress on our production capacity ramp, particularly for our 800G and 1.6Tb products').
products.size_for_company: Data center is the majority of revenue (56.1% in Q2 2026); the rest is mainly CATV (cable-TV) products.
products.competition: Coherent and Lumentum are named in the window's coverage as the closest listed peers. Large Chinese module makers (e.g., Innolight, Eoptolink) are major 800G suppliers: general industry background, not sourced in this run.
products.why_investors_care: AOI's Q3 guidance ($255-290m vs $191.9m in Q2) depends on shipping far more of these modules. On Friday, Lumentum said optical capacity is sold out through early 2029; that supports demand but says nothing about AOI's own share of it.
products.watch_next: Q3 results (estimated 2026-11-05): data-center revenue, 800G/1.6T volumes, monthly capacity versus the 650,000 target, and gross margin versus the guided 29-30.5% non-GAAP.

key_metrics.capacity: approaching 200,000 units/month; about 650,000 800G+1.6T units/month targeted by end-2026
